content:
Morning Meditation, Wed, Nov 4, 2026, 6:00 AM | Meetup
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/5093952030
6:00-6:30 Sutra study. This is more fun than it sounds. A teacher will read a short Sutra (Lesson from the Buddha) and discuss it.
6:30-7:00 Check-in. (Optional) Everyone checks in with how life is going. We have several standard questions and one wildcard question picked by a member of the group. This gets very real as this is a safe space where you can really let it all hang out.
7:00-7:30 Meditation. Thirty minutes of just sitting, observing whatever arises without judgment and without effort. If you're new to meditation, we will give some instruction.
If 6:00 a.m. is too early, please show up with you can. (If you show up after 7, you may have to wait a bit until someone sees you're in the waiting room.)
Everyone who has participated in this group has a story about how it has made their lives more peaceful. Showing up is the first step. Then just keep showing up. That's all you need to do. After some time, you may notice life getting just a bit easier.
All are welcome to be a part of our morning service. Experience not necessary. Those of any faith or lack thereof are welcome. All that is required is an open mind to learn how to promote wellness, happiness, love, and peace to oneself and all sentient beings.

content:
Morning Meditation Wake Up Together with Trina Truong, Mon, Nov 9, 2026, 6:30 AM | Meetup
Morning Meditation Wake Up Together with Trina Truong
Wake Up Together is an online meditation community that was established in 2020 by Trina Truong and partners. Our mission is to help support individuals in maintaining a solid meditation practice through practicing in an accessible and open-minded community. We meet every day, virtually. While we are rooted in the Vipassana-Insight tradition, our approach is also inclusive to all Buddhist meditation practices such as anapanasati (mindfulness of the breath), Metta (loving-kindness), body scans, Zen, ton glen, and others.
The space that our meditators come to know is one that expresses itself as welcoming and embodying all views and interpretations of spirituality.
We hold the commitment to remain humble and vulnerable in our role as the door openers to the individual's inner journey. We aspire to shape the experience for participants to experience serenity, clear-seeing and profound understanding of the mind, and the [no] self through the practices, the guidance, the teachings, and the reflections offered in group sharing.
To solidify this spiritual aspiration is to make a commitment to sit in community with a predetermined frequency or as often as you can.
We welcome you to join our beloved community!
These guided meditations are offered daily and given freely. There
are no up-front fees. Wake Up Together is 100% donation based,
relying on your support and generosity.

Explore Autism, Neurodiversity & Psychedelic Experiences, Wed, Nov 11, 2026, 6:30 PM | Meetup
Explore Autism, Neurodiversity & Psychedelic Experiences
Gather monthly to explore where our Autism, Neurodiversity and Psychedelic experiences meet, as well as how each plays out separately in our lives.
In many circles talking about autism, neurodiversity or psychedelics can be awkward or even taboo. This is our space to explore and share, unmasked. Come as you are, with your fidget toy, your quirks and special interests, and all that is uniquely you. This is an inclusive group where all are welcome, including allies.
We'll start each meeting with brief check-ins to help us get to know each other. Following will be time to chat about the topics anyone would like to discuss. Our shared purpose is to allow us to come together, be our authentic selves, and connect with others who can relate to many of our own experiences.
Suggestion - Bring some paper or a journal, and a pen, to jot down thoughts during the meeting while another person is speaking, so you remember all the brilliant thoughts you had on the topic when you get a chance to speak at the MeetUp! From experience the thoughts will spark. ;)
Our meetings are monthly online, and we occaisonally have in person events maybe 1-2 times a year, in addition to the monthly online MeetUps. In person events announced at the online meetings as they are planned.
(In person meetings - Please avoid fragranced products at our occasional in person meetings to support those with sensitivity to smells. We'll do our best to find in person meeting locations with decent lighting, and low levels of auditory distractions. Suggestions welcome on locations too!)
Be Friend is an ordained minister in a non-denominational "church without walls" for over 16 years, a late diagnosed autistic woman, and an advocate who is steeped in the newly legal psilocybin ecosystem in Oregon. She's been involved since Nov. 2022 with grassroots advocacy, encouraging our state's legislators and the Oregon Health Authority to improve the rules for the Oregon Psilocybin Services Act (OPSA).
Be has also been part of the online psychedelic communities for quite a while now and has witnessed how coming together to chat about being on the spectrum and psychedelics, can be a powerful community building space.
This event is independently organized and is not hosted, supervised, or facilitated by the Portland Psychedelic Society, a donation-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.
To learn more about Portland Psychedelic Society programming, memberships, and more, please visit our website.

content:
Zen, Psychedelics & the Path of Awakening with Ryushin Marchaj, Thu, Nov 19, 2026, 5:00 PM | Meetup
Zen, Psychedelics & the Path of Awakening with Ryushin Marchaj
Hosted by The Psychedelic Advocacy N.
Portland Psychedelic Healing and Spirituality Community
REGISTER ON OUR WEBSITE to attend this Zoom event: https://psychedelicadvocacy.org/event/zen-teacher-ryushin-marchaj-zen-and-psychedelics/
After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information and a link to join the meeting.
In this intimate and engaging talk, Ryushin will draw from decades of Zen practice and teaching, along with his personal exploration of psychedelic medicines as sacred sacraments, to explore where these two paths meet.
He’ll reflect on how Buddhist wisdom and psychedelic experience can inform one another, opening new ways of understanding the mind, awakening, suffering, and what it means to live with greater awareness, compassion, and freedom.
Together, we’ll explore how these ancient teachings and profound experiences can help us recognize conditioned patterns, deepen our understanding of ourselves, and bring greater wisdom and presence into everyday life. Ryushin brings a rare perspective that bridges traditional Zen practice with firsthand experience of psychedelic states.
Come join the conversation, bring your questions, and connect with our community as we explore what can emerge when Zen, psychedelics, and the work of integration come together.
Rev. Konrad Ryushin Marchaj is a Zen priest in the tradition of Zen Buddhism and a dharma heir of the late John Daido Loori, Roshi. Formerly the abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery in the Catskill Mountains of New York,
Born in Warsaw, Poland, he immigrated to the United States in 1967. He earned a Bachelor’s degree in Anthropology from Yale University in 1976 and a medical degree from Albany Medical College in 1980.
Ryushin began practicing Buddhism in 1983 and entered full-time residential training at Zen Mountain Monastery in 1992. During his tenure as abbot and director of operations, he also collaborated with liberal arts educators to integrate contemplative practices into higher education.
Since 2014, he has been deeply engaged in exploring ayahuasca ceremonies within diverse traditions, guided by several teachers. Integrating his medical and psychiatric background with decades of Buddhist training, Ryushin brings a compassionate, insightful, and down-to-earth approach to teaching.
**********************************************************************
Our group exists to provide education and harm reduction and foster a supportive, heart-centered community. Our group does not offer medical advice, therapy, or psychedelic substances. Also, our events do not condone or facilitate the taking of illegal drugs.

title: Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
zh_title: 币安称虚假面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币被盗
summary: 币安称虚假工作面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币抢劫 币安称虚假工作面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币抢劫 币安称虚假工作面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币抢劫 加密货币交易所币安表示，朝鲜黑客利用虚假工作面试诱骗员工安装恶意软件，最终让他们破坏公司的钱包基础设施，窃取约 63.4 亿美元的数字资产。今天发布的一份事件报告中分享了这一新信息，其中详细介绍了攻击者如何使用社交工程、恶意软件和网络攻击。
content:
币安称虚假面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币被盗
币安称虚假面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币被盗
币安称虚假面试导致 63 亿美元加密货币被盗
加密货币交易所币安表示，朝鲜黑客利用虚假面试诱骗一名员工安装恶意软件，最终让他们破坏了公司的钱包基础设施，窃取了约 63.4 亿美元的数字资产。
今天发布的一份事件报告中分享了这一新信息，该报告详细介绍了攻击者如何利用社交工程、恶意软件和受损的内部系统来实施 10 月 29 日的加密货币盗窃。
正如 BleepingComputer 之前报道的那样，FBI 将这次攻击归咎于朝鲜国家支持的黑客 TraderTraitor，也被追踪为 Lazarus Group、Jade Sleet 和 APT38。
币安表示，此次攻击始于 9 月份，当时有人冒充一家虚构公司的项目总监，通过合法的求职平台联系了一名软件工程师。
该员工的个人资料引用了他在币安的经历，这使他成为寻求破坏加密货币交易所的攻击者的重要目标。
假招聘人员为该员工安排了两次面试，首先是一个冒充人力资源代表的人，然后是另一个自称是公司首席执行官的人。
在第一次采访中，虚假的人力资源代表进行了实时视频通话，并分享了带有个人照片和视频的社交媒体账号，以建立信任。第二次面试是通过一个流行的社交聊天应用程序进行的，该应用程序指示员工从在线代码库下载编码作业。根据币安的说法，存储库包含恶意代码，这些代码在执行时会以防病毒软件未检测到的以前看不见的自定义恶意软件入侵员工的设备。币安解释说： “恶意软件采用了复杂的混淆和规避技术，包括用恶意版本替换合法的开发工具组件，以执行命令并与攻击者控制的外部服务器建立通信。”“当时端点安全保护工具未检测到0天恶意软件。攻击者还采取措施隐藏恶意活动并删除受损痕迹，使检测和后续调查更具挑战性。”
币安解释说，恶意脚本在macOS Homebrew安装目录中创建了一个名为pyenv_的替换可执行文件。然后，该脚本删除了合法的pyenv可执行文件，将恶意文件重命名为pyenv ，修改了其符号链接，并使用它来生成Z shell （ zsh ）进程。恶意替换允许攻击者执行从攻击者控制的服务器接收的命令。
到 10 月 20 日，攻击者利用受感染工程师的计算机和内部人工智能工具，对币安钱包基础设施上工作的另外两名员工进行了攻击，获取了凭据和容器部署令牌。
10 月 29 日，黑客利用窃取的凭证部署恶意脚本，并获得对币安钱包签名服务的未经授权的访问，从而使他们能够跨多个区块链转移数十亿美元的加密货币。
攻击者还滥用了以太坊的EIP-7702授权机制，使他们即使在交易所暂停后仍能继续窃取加密货币

【原文 English Original】
Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says North Korean hackers used a fake job interview to trick an employee into installing malware that ultimately let them compromise the company's wallet infrastructure and steal about $6.34 billion in digital assets.
This new information was shared in an incident report published today, which details how the attackers used social engineering, malicious software, and compromised internal systems to carry out the October 29 crypto theft.
As previously reported by BleepingComputer, the FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38.
Binance says the attack began in September when a software engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone impersonating a Project Director at a fictitious company.
The employee's profile referenced his experience at Binance, making him a valuable target for attackers looking to breach the cryptocurrency exchange.
The fake recruiter scheduled two interviews for the employee, first with someone posing as a human resources representative, then with another individual claiming to be the company's CEO.
During the first interview, the fake HR representative held a live video call and shared a social media account with personal photos and videos to build trust.
The second interview took place through a popular social chat application where the employee was instructed to download a coding assignment from an online code repository.
According to Binance, the repository contained malicious code that, when executed, compromised the employee's device with previously unseen custom malware that antivirus software did not detect.
"The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server," explained Binance.
"The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging."
Binance explained that the malicious script created a replacement executable named pyenv_ in the macOS Homebrew installation directory.
The script then deleted the legitimate pyenv executable, renamed the malicious file to pyenv, modified its symbolic link, and used it to spawn a Z shell (zsh) process.
The malicious replacement allowed the attackers to execute commands received from an attacker-controlled server.
By October 20, the attackers had used the compromised engineer's computer and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional employees working on Binance's wallet infrastructure, obtaining credentials and a container deployment token.
On October 29, the hackers used the stolen credentials to deploy a malicious script and gain unauthorized access to Binance's wallet signing service, allowing them to transfer billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains.
The attackers also abused Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism, allowing them to continue stealing cryptocurrency even after the exchange suspended withdrawals.
Binance says it has since rebuilt affected systems, replaced compromised devices, and revoked stolen credentials.
As of November 3, approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of October 31.
Binance says it is continuing to investigate the breach and has brought in independent security firms to review its findings.
Fake job interviews that lead to malware installs are a common tactic in North Korean hacking campaigns known as Contagious Interview and Operation Dream Job. These campaigns use fake job offers and interviews to trick developers and cryptocurrency employees into installing malware.
In June 2025, cybersecurity firm Socket reported that a Contagious Interview campaign impersonated recruiters on LinkedIn and sent developers coding assignments containing malicious npm packages.
As part of these attacks, the hackers distributed 35 malicious npm packages that installed malware, allowing them to steal browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and other information from infected computers.
North Korean Lazarus hackers have also used similar tactics in Operation Dream Job, distributing malware disguised as employment documents to people working in software development and DeFi companies.
While Binance has not linked the employee compromise to either specific campaign, the use of a fake recruiter, multiple interviews, and a malicious coding assignment closely mirrors these previously documented North Korean tactics.

title: WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app
zh_title: WorkOS 称攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 破坏内部销售应用程序
summary: WorkOS 表示，攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 攻破内部销售应用程序 WorkOS 表示，攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 攻破内部销售应用程序 WorkOS 表示，攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 攻破内部销售应用程序 开发者平台 WorkOS 在威胁行为者访问业务联系记录和客户通信摘要后遭受数据泄露。据该公司称，攻击者使用人工智能进攻性安全框架来自动进行侦察和利用尝试。根据调查证据，没有 WorkOS 应用程序数据或生产服务被访问或受到影响。 WorkOS 是一个开发者
content:
WorkOS 称攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 破坏内部销售应用程序
WorkOS 称攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 破坏内部销售应用程序
WorkOS 称攻击者使用 ARTEX AI 破坏内部销售应用程序
在威胁行为者访问业务联系记录和客户通信摘要后，开发者平台 WorkOS 遭受了数据泄露。
据该公司称，攻击者使用人工智能进攻性安全框架来自动进行侦察和利用尝试。
根据调查证据，没有 WorkOS 应用程序数据或生产服务被访问或受到影响。
WorkOS 是一家开发基础设施公司，提供 API、SDK 和工具，用于将企业身份验证、单点登录 (SSO)、用户管理和身份管理等服务集成到应用程序中。
据其网站称，至少有 3000 家公司使用其服务，包括 OpenAI、Anthropic、Cursor、Perplexity、Snowflake、Plaid、Webglow 和 Netlify。
该公司在事件警报中表示：“2026 年 10 月 30 日，我们发现对我们销售团队使用的内部 WorkOS 应用程序进行了未经授权的访问。”
业务联系详细信息（CRM 系统中的姓名、电子邮件地址、职位和公司隶属关系）
客户帐户历史记录（产品使用情况和连接或目录运行状况）
客户沟通（销售电话、支持讨论和客户 Slack 对话的摘要和摘录）
企业帐户和关系信息（帐户历史记录、有关销售和客户关系的信息）
检测到入侵后，WorkOS 禁用了对受影响应用程序的外部访问，并审查了其对内部工具的访问控制。
该公司还与一家独立的取证和事件响应公司签约，以跟踪未经授权的活动并确定其全面影响。
该公司承诺直接通知受影响的客户，并警告用户对利用暴露信息的网络钓鱼或社会工程尝试保持警惕。
WorkOS 的声明称，此次攻击使用了人工智能驱动的进攻性安全框架来自动执行侦察和利用尝试。
公司创始人 Michael Grinich 分享了更多细节，称攻击者使用了 ARTEX AI 渗透测试套件，该套件已在今年的多起事件中观察到。
该平台于今年早些时候由中国开发商发布，作为进攻性安全的开源项目提供。
ARTEX AI 在被用于针对韩国银行的攻击后被私有化，但其代码的几个分支仍然可用。
最近，CrowdStrike 透露网络间谍组织“Vapor Panda”在针对 200 个组织的全球活动中使用了渗透测试框架。

Developer platform WorkOS suffered a data breach after a threat actor accessed business contact records and summaries of customer communications.
According to the company, the attacker used an AI offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.

WorkOS is a developer infrastructure company that provides APIs, SDKs, and tools for integrating services such as enterprise authentication, single sign-on (SSO), user management, and identity management into applications.
According to its website, at least 3,000 companies use its services, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Perplexity, Snowflake, Plaid, Webglow, and Netlify.
“On October 30, 2026, we identified unauthorized access to an internal WorkOS application used by our sales team,” the company says in an incident alert.
Business contact details (names, email addresses, job titles, and company affiliations from the CRM systems)
Customer account histories (product usage and connection or directory health)
Customer communications (summaries and excerpts from sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations)
Business account and relationship information (account histories, information about sales and customer relationship)
After detecting the intrusion, WorkOS disabled external access to the affected application and reviewed its access controls on internal tools.
The company also contracted an independent forensics and incident response firm to track the unauthorized activity and determine its full impact.
The company promised to notify affected customers directly, and warned its users to remain vigilant for phishing or social engineering attempts leveraging the exposed information.
WorkOS’s announcement says the attack used an AI-powered offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.
Company founder Michael Grinich shared more details, saying that the attacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite that has been observed in multiple incidents this year.
Released earlier this year by Chinese developers, the platform was available as an open-source project for offensive security.
ARTEX AI became private after it was used in attacks targeting South Korean banks, but several forks of its code are still available.
More recently, CrowdStrike revealed that cyber-espionage group “Vapor Panda” used the pentesting framework in a global campaign targeting 200 organizations.
Previously, the non-profit cybersecurity organization DIVD also revealed that the same framework powered the attacks it suffered last September.
Grinich explained that the investigating team identified user agents such as ‘artex-enrich/1.0’ and ‘norma/0.4’ in web requests from the threat actor.

10月28日，台湾媒体报道，罗马教廷国务秘书保罗·理查德·加拉格尔大主教在罗马与记者举行的活动中谈到了梵蒂冈驻华办事处的谈判进展情况。当记者询问这些谈判的进展情况时，加拉格尔主教回答说：“我们的想法是在北京拥有某种文化存在。但是，就像谈判中的所有事情一样，需要付出代价，而目前我们不愿意付出这个代价。”
该报道引起了台湾和香港媒体的高度关注。部分原因是它援引意大利《晚邮报》此前的报道称，已故教宗方济各在任期间，梵蒂冈国务秘书处多次表达了在中国设立“常设办事处”的愿望。 《晚邮报》还指出，北京方面提出了一个前提条件，要求梵蒂冈首先与台湾断交。
台湾新闻媒体《ETtoday》跟进报道，标题为“北京提议‘与台湾断交’以换取职位？梵蒂冈外长：暂时不准备付出代价”。与此同时，香港无线电视台发表了题为《梵蒂冈外长：中梵主教协议有缺陷，罗马教廷无意在北京设立办事处》的深度报道。加拉格尔总主教关于设立办事处的言论，无疑触动了两岸关系的敏感神经。
然而，虽然加拉格尔大主教提到“需要付出代价”，但他没有明确说明这个“代价”意味着什么。 INFOVATICANA的一份报告简单地指出，“大主教不想具体说明达成这样的谅解需要什么条件。目前，罗马教廷与台湾保持外交关系，并在香港设有考察团，但在中华人民共和国没有正式外交代表。”
路透社的报道仅聚焦于加拉格尔承认临时协议的缺陷，并援引他的话说：“这并不容易，对话也不容易。协议的缺陷是显而易见的，但我们承诺坚持对话……这就是将继续发生的事情。”
对比中英文媒体的报道，所谓罗马教廷必须付出（但目前不愿意）与台湾断交的“代价”，似乎是华文媒体对意大利过往报道的解读，这也反映了中共领导的政府的表态。
除了台湾和中国之间就梵蒂冈正式承认问题进行的政治操弄之外，罗马教廷在中国设立办事处的真正动机是什么？是为了建立外交关系吗

On October 28, Taiwanese media reported that the Secretary for Relations with States of the Holy See, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, addressed the progress of negotiations regarding a Vatican office in China at an event with journalists in Rome. When a reporter asked about the status of these talks, Monsignor Gallagher responded: “The idea is to have some type of cultural presence in Beijing. But, as with everything in a negotiation, there would be a price to pay and, for the moment, we are not willing to pay that price.”
The report drew significant attention in Taiwan and Hong Kong media. This was partly because it cited earlier reporting by the Italian daily Corriere della Sera that, during the tenure of the late Pope Francis, the Vatican’s Secretariat of State repeatedly expressed a long-standing desire to establish a “permanent office” in China. Corriere della Sera also noted that Beijing proposed a precondition, demanding that the Vatican first sever diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
The Taiwanese news outlet ETtoday followed up, using the headline, “Beijing Proposes ‘Severing Ties with Taiwan’ in Exchange for an Office? Vatican Foreign Minister: Not Prepared to Pay the Price for Now.” Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s TVB provided an in-depth report headlined, “Vatican Foreign Minister: Sino-Vatican Bishop Agreement Flawed, Holy See Has No Intention of Setting Up Office in Beijing.” Archbishop Gallagher’s remarks about establishing an office have undoubtedly struck a sensitive nerve in cross-strait relations.
However, while Archbishop Gallagher mentioned that “there would be a price to pay,” he did not explicitly state what that “price” entails. A report by INFOVATICANA simply noted, “The archbishop did not wish to specify what the demands would be to reach such an understanding. Currently, the Holy See maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan and has a study mission in Hong Kong, but does not have official diplomatic representation in the People’s Republic of China.”
Reuters’ reporting focused solely on Gallagher’s admission of the provisional agreement’s flaws, quoting him as saying: “It’s not easy, the dialogue is not easy. The imperfections of the agreement are evident, but there is a commitment to persevere in dialogue… and that is what will continue to happen.”
Comparing Chinese and English media reports, the assertion that the “price” the Holy See must pay – but is currently unwilling to – involves severing ties with Taiwan seems to be an interpretation by Chinese-language media of past Italian reporting, which in turn reflected the Chinese Communist Party-led government’s stated position.
Beyond the political maneuvering between Taiwan and China over formal Vatican recognition, what is the Holy See’s real motive for establishing an office in China? Is it to forge diplomatic relations, or is it a procedural step in negotiating the agreement on the appointment of bishops?
I believe it is necessary to clarify the significance of this “office” through the lens of the Holy See’s pastoral mechanism for China – specifically, the appointment of bishops. The Vatican’s effort to establish a presence in Beijing should not be oversimplified as “the Holy See rejecting China’s demand to break ties with Taiwan” or “the Holy See currently having no intention of opening an office in Beijing.”
As to whether this issue will return to the Sino-Vatican negotiating table, some scholars believe that the issue of setting up an office is unlikely to be discussed in near-term negotiations, now that the policy position is clear. I disagree; establishing an “office” will almost certainly remain an active topic of discussion. My primary argument is that an on-the-ground presence is necessary to properly implement the Sino-Vatican agreement. A Papal delegate’s presence in Beijing is necessary for good governance over the episcopal appointment process. Beijing is deliberately misinterpreting the purpose of this “office” as a matter of diplomatic negotiation over cross-strait relations, masking its true reluctance to loosen its control over the Catholic Church’s religious freedom.
While traveling in a devoutly Catholic European country, I had the privilege of attending its National Day reception. During the event, I met a senior Holy See diplomat assigned to that nation. Out of curiosity, I asked, “Father, what does your daily work entail? Being in such a devout Catholic country, is your work fairly smooth?” The diplomat replied, “Not exactly. 90 percent of my work involves investigating bishop appointments. I need to understand the backgrounds of so many clergy members to determine who is suitable to become a bishop.” This Holy See diplomat’s statement truthfully outlined the core mission of a papal diplomat. Fulfilling pastoral care in a local Catholic Church includes vetting candidates for the episcopacy as a primary task.
The Holy See and the People’s Republic of China signed a provisional agreement on the appointment of bishops in 2018, and renewed it in 2024 for another four years, until 2028. Since the signing of the agreement, the Pope has appointed several bishops in China, resulting in an increasingly rejuvenated Chinese Catholic episcopate. However, the process by which China selects bishop candidates remains a black box. Because there is no true religious freedom in China, the Catholic Church remains under severe control of the Chinese Communist Party’s United Front Work Department.
Scholars note that, even without a formal Holy See-Vatican office in China, certain civic organizations operated by religious orders may play intermediary roles. Yet these unofficial mechanisms are far less institutionalized than establishing a direct, official office in Beijing. Regarding the Holy See’s process for selecting bishop candidates, a significant concern is whether the background of every episcopal candidate can be vetted in a diverse and transparent manner. If the Holy See does not have an official delegate in China – and if that representative cannot investigate freely while possessing completely uncontrolled personal liberty – then establishing a Holy See-Vatican office in Beijing is a false proposition, one that merely falls into the CCP’s diplomatic narrative of coercing the Holy See over whether to sever ties with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
In the article “Diplomacy and Divided Nations: The Holy See’s Approach to China and Taiwan,” published in the journal Issues & Studies, Yun Wang and I analyzed the distinction between a Papal Delegation and an Apostolic Nunciature. The core differences lie in the presence of “Diplomatic Recognition” and whether the primary counterpart for engagement is the “local government” or the “local church.” These two terms represent entirely different tiers of diplomatic tools the Vatican uses across varying political environments and historical periods. Whether the Holy See-Vatican is pushing to establish a Papal Delegation or an Apostolic Nunciature in Beijing becomes clearer when we look at another Asian communist state the Holy See engages with: Vietnam.
The office in Beijing is truly intended to be a Papal Delegation, an ecclesiastical rather than diplomatic office. However, the CCP cleverly conflates the two. When the Holy See proposes a Papal Delegation to China, Beijing counters that establishing an Apostolic Nunciature requires “first severing ties with Taipei.” This is a malicious interpretation to disguise China’s basic lack of religious freedom.
This year marks the 400th anniversary of Catholicism’s arrival in Taiwan. The Chargé d’Affaires of the Apostolic Nunciature to China (Taipei), Monsignor Stefano Mazzotti, has attended multiple events marking the anniversary. “This year marks the 400th anniversary of the arrival of the first Catholic missionaries in Taiwan to evangelize,” he said in one such speech. “Today, the Catholic Church has taken deep root and become an indispensable part of Taiwan’s diverse society. The Holy See will work hand in hand with the international community, including Taiwan, to continue to develop and consolidate the Church’s mission within the framework of ‘security and freedom,’”
As my previous article “Taiwan-Vatican Ties: The Dynamic Interplay Under Pope Leo XIV” indicated, amid shifting Sino-Vatican dynamics, Taiwan has no reason to worry. In the eyes of the Holy See, Taiwan remains an undeniably “precious” presence. I firmly believe Taiwan can be decoupled from the Sino-Vatican negotiation narrative, and indeed, it must be. Neither Taiwan nor the Holy See should fall into the narrative trap maliciously set by the Chinese Communist Party.

title: ACM Research Announces Shipment of Its First 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p Panel-Level Horizontal Electroplating Production Tool
zh_title: ACM Research 宣布发货其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具
summary: 半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级加工越来越受到关注
content:
半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级处理因其适应更大基板的能力而在整个行业中受到关注。电镀是先进封装制造中最关键的步骤之一，其中设备稳定性、镀层厚度均匀性和一致性对于成功的工艺集成、产品良率和制造效率至关重要。新发货的工具专为 310 × 310 mm 面板级应用而设计，展示了 ACM 根据客户要求快速推进产品开发的能力。在此之前，ACM 首款 515 × 510 mm 研发工具于去年发货，突显了 ACM 将技术突破快速商业化至规模生产的能力。 “这是 ACM 先进封装工作的一个重要里程碑，标志着我们向亚洲客户交付了世界上第一个 310 × 310 毫米面板级水平电镀生产工具，”ACM 博士说。
ACM Research 总裁兼首席执行官 David Wang 表示：“我们相信，我们专有的水平电镀技术具有独特的优势，能够实现跨多种面板尺寸和新兴封装架构的下一代先进半导体封装。随着人工智能推动日益复杂的封装要求，我们看到了 ACM 在这个快速发展的市场中发挥推动作用的重要长期机会。” Ultra ECP ap-p 系统采用 ACM 专有的水平电镀技术，支持铜 (Cu)、镍 (Ni)、锡银 (SnAg) 和金 (Au) 电镀工艺。其铜电镀室采用专为高铜柱应用设计的高速电镀桨，能够在高电镀速率下为 300 微米铜柱实现良好的芯片内均匀性。该系统还具有四面密封干接触吸盘，可提高可靠性；单元内冲洗功能可最大限度地减少不同电镀单元之间的化学交叉污染；水平电镀设计采用 ACM 正在申请专利的技术，使吸盘的旋转与旋转矩形电场同步，从而实现卓越的沉积均匀性。除了设备交付之外，ACM 还致力于通过提供高质量设备、支持可靠的批量生产和提供可靠的技术支持来建立长期的客户关系。
ACM将继续推进技术进步，拓展多产品平台，扩大全球客户群。ACM旨在通过与全球合作伙伴的合作，支持人工智能行业的发展，并以其差异化的半导体设备技术为客户创造更大的价值。 ACM Research 宣布其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具发货的消息首先出现在《半导体文摘》上。

【原文 English Original】
ACM Research, Inc. , a supplier of wafer processing solutions for semiconductor and advanced packaging applications, today announced the shipment of its first 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p panel-level horizontal electroplating production system to a customer in Asia outside mainland China. The shipment marks another significant advance in ACM’s core panel-level technologies and represents an important step forward in broadening its multi-product platform and expanding its global customer presence. As advanced packaging technologies continue to evolve, panel-level processing is gaining traction across the industry for its ability to accommodate larger substrates. Electroplating is one of the most critical steps in advanced packaging manufacturing, where equipment stability, plating thickness uniformity and consistency are essential to successful process integration, product yield and manufacturing efficiency. The newly shipped tool is designed for 310 × 310 mm panel-level applications, and demonstrates ACM’s ability to quickly advance product development per customer requirements. This follows last year’s shipment of ACM’s first 515 × 510 mm R&D tool, highlighting ACM’s ability to rapidly commercialize technical breakthroughs into scale production. “This is an important milestone for ACM’s advanced packaging efforts, and marks shipment of what we believe is the world’s first 310 × 310 mm panel-level horizontal electroplating production tool to a customer in Asia,” said Dr. David Wang, President and Chief Executive Officer of ACM Research. “We believe our proprietary horizontal plating technology is uniquely positioned to enable the next generation of advanced semiconductor packaging across multiple panel sizes and emerging packaging architectures. As AI drives increasingly complex packaging requirements, we see a significant long-term opportunity for ACM to play an enabling role in this rapidly evolving market.” The Ultra ECP ap-p system features ACM’s proprietary horizontal electroplating technology and supports copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), tin-silver (SnAg) and gold (Au) plating processes. Its copper plating chamber incorporates a high-speed plating paddle specifically designed for tall copper pillar applications, capable of achieving good within-die uniformity for 300-micron copper pillars at high plating rates. The system also features a four-sided sealing dry contact chuck for improved reliability, in-cell rinse functionality to minimize chemical cross-contamination between different plating cells, and a horizontal electroplating design that uses ACM’s patent-pending technology to synchronize the rotation of the chuck with a rotating rectangular electric field for superior deposition uniformity. Beyond equipment delivery, ACM is committed to building long-term customer relationships by providing high-quality equipment, supporting reliable volume production and delivering reliable technical support. ACM will continue to advance its technologies, expand its multi-product platform and grow its global customer base. Through collaboration with partners worldwide, ACM aims to support the growth of the AI industry and create greater value for customers with its differentiated semiconductor equipment technologies.
