Monday, 2 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong reports six new Legionnaires' disease cases in one week
Hong Kong's Department of Health reported six community-acquired Legionnaires' disease cases from 25 to 31 October, involving men aged 48 to 78 in various districts. The centre said the cases are sporadic with no epidemiological link to previous cases, bringing the 2026 total to 169.
Hong Kong's Department of Health reported six new community-acquired cases of Legionnaires' disease in the week from 25 to 31 October, involving six men aged between 48 and 78. The patients resided in Wan Chai, Yau Tsim Mong, Southern, Sha Tin and Tai Po districts, the department said in a statement on 2 November.
The Centre for Health Protection has launched epidemiological investigations to identify possible sources of infection and high-risk exposure factors. Preliminary findings indicated the cases are sporadic, with no evidence linking them to other confirmed cases previously recorded in Hong Kong, the centre said.
As of 31 October, a total of 169 Legionnaires' disease cases have been recorded in Hong Kong this year, compared with 167 in 2025 and 135 in 2024, according to the department.
The department noted that men, people aged over 50, smokers, heavy drinkers and those with weakened immune systems are more susceptible to Legionnaires' disease. Other risk factors include poorly maintained water supply systems, use of old water systems in homes, proximity to cooling towers or fountains, use of electric water heaters, spas or hot springs, and recent stays in hotels or on ships.
Legionella bacteria can thrive in various environments, particularly in warm water between 20 and 45 degrees Celsius. Sources include water tanks, hot and cold water systems, cooling towers, spas, fountains, humidifiers and home respiratory medical equipment. Infection can occur through inhaling contaminated water droplets or mist from human-made water systems, and also when handling garden soil, compost or potting mix.
The department advised immunocompromised individuals to use sterile or boiled water for drinking, brushing teeth and rinsing; avoid using humidifiers or other mist-producing devices; and, if using such devices, to use sterile water or freshly boiled cooled tap water rather than direct tap water. It also urged regular cleaning and maintenance according to manufacturers' instructions.
The department also called on the public not to smoke and to avoid alcohol, and provided contact details for its smoking cessation hotline and an alcohol screening and brief intervention tool for primary healthcare providers.

content:
香港交易所将于三月起延长收市后衍生品交易 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
港交所将于三月起延长收盘后衍生品交易
香港交易及结算所计划从 3 月份起将收盘后衍生品交易时间延长 1 小时 15 分钟，尚待监管部门批准。 11 月份正在考虑进一步延长至凌晨 5:15。该交易所还计划与香港金管局进行数字货币试点，用于境外保证金存款
香港交易及结算所（香港交易所）宣布，计划从明年 3 月起延长衍生品收盘后交易时段，但须获得监管机构批准和市场准备就绪。
根据新安排，盘后交易时段的收盘时间将从凌晨3点推迟至凌晨4点15分。该交易所表示，将根据初步延期后的市场发展情况，考虑进一步延期至明年11月凌晨5点15分。
香港交易所首席运营官刘贝蒂表示，全球市场的联系日益紧密，投资者需要更大的灵活性来应对不同时区的市场变化并管理风险。该交易所希望新措施以及之前宣布的使用数字货币进行保证金存款的试点计划将促进市场参与并增强服务和运营弹性。
香港交易所正与香港金融管理局（金管局）合作开展一项试点计划，探索在银行营业时间以外使用数字港元（e-HKD）支付保证金，为市​​场参与者在收市后交易时段提供更灵活的支付选择。实施细则将适时另行公布。

Monday, 2 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
HK Exchange to extend post-close derivatives trading from March
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing plans to extend post-close derivatives trading by one hour 15 minutes from March, pending regulatory approval. A further extension to 5:15am is being considered for November. The exchange also plans a digital-currency pilot with the HKMA for margin deposits outside b
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) has announced plans to extend the post-close trading session for derivatives from March next year, subject to regulatory approval and market readiness.
Under the new arrangement, the closing time of the after-hours trading session would be pushed back from 3am to 4:15am. The exchange said it would consider a further extension to 5:15am in November next year, depending on market development after the initial extension.
HKEX Chief Operating Officer Betty Lau said global markets are becoming increasingly interconnected, and investors need greater flexibility to respond to market changes across different time zones and to manage risk. The exchange hopes the new measures, together with a previously announced pilot scheme using digital currency for margin deposits, will facilitate market participation and enhance service and operational resilience.
HKEX is working with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) on a pilot programme exploring the use of a digital Hong Kong dollar (e-HKD) for margin payments outside banking hours, offering market participants more flexible payment options during the post-close trading session. Details of the implementation will be announced separately in due course.

香港房屋委员会公布华富村重建及人工智能交通计划 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港房屋委员会公布华富村重建及人工智能交通计划
香港房屋委员会向南区区议会汇报华富村重建及华富村新公屋第一期工程，获得广泛支持。第一个接待屋村华富北将于今年竣工，居民将于 2027 年第三季度入住。当局计划采用人工智能技术
香港房屋委员会于11月2日向南区区议会通报华富村重建及搬迁计划的最新进展，并就华富村新公营房屋发展第一期征求议员意见，获普遍支持。
第一个落成的接待屋村，位于华径街的华富北，将于今年年底竣工。华安楼及华乐楼的住户将陆续入住，预计于2027年第三季完成搬迁。新华富村第一期工程随后将开始拆迁，较原计划提早六年接纳华翠楼及华景楼的住户。
为帮助受第一期b期清拆影响的住户，即华祥楼、华健楼及华泰楼的住户，当局将推出一项早期搬迁计划，将华富北的400多个单位纳入其中。成功申请者预计将于 2027 年 3 月入住。其他四个接待屋村将于 2028 年至 2031 年间竣工。
新华富村采用“社区为本”的核心设计理念。通过“十种华府”公众参与计划，设计团队收集了利益相关者的意见，并制定了四项策略：保育与活化、社区建设、可持续发展和创新技术。该局将利用数字信息管理和数据分析平台，对关键工程和环境参数进行模拟和分析。当局亦正与路政署铁路发展部及港铁公司就南港岛线（西段）路线及华富站选址进行协调。总体规划设计预计2028年上半年基本完成。
新华富村第一期以「重建华富」为主题，拟建三座住宅楼，供华翠楼及华景楼居民居住。它将保护和振兴现有的华富（1）购物中心和外面的“悦榕庄头”，延续原来的“市中心”概念。该计划包括社会福利设施、室外庭院、有顶公共空间和华富历史档案馆。华富路的部分路段将会重新调整。当局预计于 2027 年初公布相关道路工程，并于 2028 年中开始施工。
土木工程拓展署薄扶林南的行人及道路改善工程预计于2027年完成。港铁公司正为南港岛线（西段）进行详细规划及设计，计划于2034年通车。当局正与香港大学的研究团队合作开发综合智能监控平台，利用人工智能和实时交通数据动态规划施工车辆路线

Monday, 2 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong Housing Authority unveils Wah Fu Estate redevelopment, AI traffic plan
Hong Kong Housing Authority briefs Southern District Council on Wah Fu Estate redevelopment and first phase of new Wah Fu Estate public housing, gaining broad support. The first reception estate, Wah Fu North, will finish this year, with residents moving in by Q3 2027. The authority plans AI-powered
Hong Kong's Housing Authority on 2 November briefed the Southern District Council on the latest progress of the Wah Fu Estate redevelopment and relocation plan, and sought councillors' views on the first phase of the new Wah Fu Estate public housing development, receiving general support.
The first completed reception estate, Wah Fu North on Wah Keng Street, will finish construction by the end of this year. Residents of Wah On House and Wah Lok House will gradually move in, with relocation expected to be completed by the third quarter of 2027. Demolition will then begin to make way for the first phase of the new Wah Fu Estate, enabling it to receive residents of Wah Chui House and Wah King House six years earlier than originally planned.
To help households affected by phase 1b clearance – those in Wah Cheung House, Wah Kin House and Wah Tai House – the authority is offering an early relocation scheme with more than 400 flats at Wah Fu North. Successful applicants are expected to move in by March 2027. The other four reception estates will be completed between 2028 and 2031.
The new Wah Fu Estate adopts a 'community-based' core design concept. Through the 'Ten Kinds of Wah Fu' public participation programme, the design team has gathered stakeholder views and developed four strategies: conservation and revitalisation, community building, sustainable development, and innovative technology. The authority will use digital information management and data analysis platforms to simulate and analyse key engineering and environmental parameters. The authority is also coordinating with the Highways Department's Railway Development Division and MTR Corporation on the South Island Line (West Section) alignment and Wah Fu station location. Overall planning and design are expected to be largely completed by the first half of 2028.
The first phase of the new Wah Fu Estate, themed 'Rebuilding Wah Fu', proposes three residential towers for Wah Chui House and Wah King House residents. It will conserve and revitalise the existing Wah Fu (1) Shopping Centre and the 'Banyan Tree Head' outside, continuing the original 'town centre' concept. The plan includes social welfare facilities, outdoor courtyards, covered public spaces and a Wah Fu history archive. Part of Wah Fu Road will be realigned. The authority expects to gazette related road works in early 2027 and begin construction by mid-2028.
The Civil Engineering and Development Department's pedestrian and road improvement works in Pok Fu Lam South are expected to finish in 2027. MTR Corporation is conducting detailed planning and design for the South Island Line (West Section), which is scheduled to open by 2034. The authority is collaborating with a research team from the University of Hong Kong to develop an integrated smart monitoring platform, using artificial intelligence and real-time traffic data to dynamically plan construction vehicle routes, aiming to reduce traffic impact on surrounding areas.

香港旅游发展局推出十一月美食月 逾400家食肆齐聚中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港旅游发展局推出十一月美食月 逾400间食肆齐聚
香港旅游发展局于 11 月推出美食月，超过 400 家餐厅和酒吧提供特别优惠。亮点包括包含 100 个场所的深夜美食地图以及旅游热点的延长营业时间。组织者的目标是促进当地支出和社区探索。
香港旅游发展局（旅发局）推出「香港美食月」，为期整个十一月，全城超过 400 间餐厅、酒吧及食店提供限时餐饮优惠。
该计划包括连接100家餐厅和酒吧的“香港深夜美食地图”，晚上9点后将提供独家优惠。一些热门旅游区的参与商店将延长营业时间至午夜或更晚。
刚刚结束的“香港美酒佳肴巡礼”的参加者还可凭活动中派发的“香港美食月尊享礼遇卡”，获得超过250项额外优惠。其中包括套餐折扣、餐饮折扣、迎宾饮品、买一送一优惠和活动兑换。
旅发局主席林建岳表示，是次活动旨在连接星级餐厅、地方风味餐厅、特色酒吧和深夜热点等五个主题类别，让游客和居民在整个11月从早到晚都能享受到香港的美食魅力。他表示希望这项活动能够鼓励更多人探索当地社区并在香港消费。

Hong Kong Tourism Board launches November Food Month with over 400 eateries
The Hong Kong Tourism Board launches Food Month in November, with over 400 restaurants and bars offering special deals. Highlights include a late-night food map with 100 venues and extended hours at tourist hotspots. Organisers aim to boost local spending and community exploration.
The Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB) has launched “Hong Kong Food Month”, running throughout November, with more than 400 restaurants, bars and food outlets across the city offering limited-time food and beverage promotions.
The initiative includes a “Hong Kong Late-Night Food Map” linking 100 restaurants and bars, which will offer exclusive deals after 9pm. Some participating outlets in popular tourist areas will extend their opening hours until midnight or later.
Attendees of the recently concluded “Hong Kong Wine and Food Festival” can also use the “Hong Kong Food Month Exclusive Privilege Card” distributed at the event to access more than 250 additional benefits. These include discounts on set menus, dining discounts, welcome drinks, buy-one-get-one-free offers and activity redemptions.
HKTB chairman Peter Lam said the event aims to connect five themed categories—star-rated restaurants, regional eateries, specialty bars and late-night hotspots—so that both tourists and residents can enjoy the city’s culinary appeal from day to night throughout November. He expressed hope the campaign would encourage more people to explore local communities and spend in Hong Kong.

content:
The Weeknd 在香港最后一场演出中向甄子丹致敬，佩戴 DonniEYE 太阳镜 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
The Weeknd 在香港最后一场演出中向甄子丹致敬，佩戴 DonniEYE 太阳镜
加拿大歌手 The Weeknd 在启德体育场结束了他的“After Hours Til Dawn 巡回演唱会”，向香港动作明星甄子丹致敬，在“Take My Breath”中戴着甄子丹时尚品牌 DonniEYE 的太阳镜。
据《标准报》报道，加拿大歌手 The Weeknd 在启德大球场结束了他的四场“After Hours Til Dawn 巡回演唱会”，并向香港动作偶像甄子丹致敬。
在表演他的热门歌曲《Take My Breath》时，The Weeknd 佩戴了甄子丹个人时尚品牌 DonniEYE 的太阳镜，令现场观众大吃一惊。甄子丹女儿甄子丹分享的视频片段显示，这位动作明星戴着帽子，穿着黑色皮夹克，挥舞着拳头，随着音乐跳舞。
DonniEYE 由甄子丹于 2018 年创立，品牌名称源自甄子丹的英文名，每双眼镜都旨在体现甄子丹本人所倡导的正能量和观点。
近年来，该品牌推出了多款备受瞩目的产品，引起了轰动。甄子丹在大片《疾速追杀：第四章》中饰演盲人刺客凯恩后，DonniEYE 蔡司镜片系列引起了全球关注。
继甄子丹出演 2016 年电影《侠盗一号：星球大战外传》后，DonniEYE 于 2023 年与星球大战系列合作推出官方联名系列。该系列采用五种受角色启发的设计，包括 C-3PO、R2-D2、达斯·维达、冲锋队和波巴·费特，将流行文化与品牌的标志性美学融为一体。

The Weeknd honours Donnie Yen with DonniEYE sunglasses at final Hong Kong show
Canadian singer The Weeknd wrapped up his 'After Hours Til Dawn Tour' at Kai Tak Stadium with a tribute to Hong Kong action star Donnie Yen, wearing sunglasses from Yen's fashion brand DonniEYE during 'Take My Breath.'
Canadian singer The Weeknd concluded his four-show 'After Hours Til Dawn Tour' at Kai Tak Stadium with a special tribute to Hong Kong action icon Donnie Yen Chi-tan, according to The Standard.
While performing his hit track 'Take My Breath,' The Weeknd surprised the crowd by wearing a pair of sunglasses from Yen's personal fashion brand, DonniEYE. Video footage shared by Yen's daughter Jasmine Yen showed the action star dressed in a hat and a black leather jacket, pumping his fists and dancing along to the music.
DonniEYE was founded by Donnie Yen in 2018. The brand's name derives from the actor's English name, and each pair is designed to project the positive energy and outlook championed by Yen himself.
The brand has generated buzz with several high-profile releases in recent years. The DonniEYE Zeiss Lenses Collection drew global attention after Yen wore the shades throughout his role as the blind assassin Caine in the blockbuster film John Wick: Chapter 4.
In 2023, DonniEYE collaborated with the Star Wars franchise to launch an official co-branded collection, following Yen's appearance in the 2016 film Rogue One: A Star Wars Story. This collection features five character-inspired designs, including C-3PO, R2-D2, Darth Vader, Stormtrooper, and Boba Fett, blending pop culture with the brand's signature aesthetic.

summary: 香港特首与教育部长讨论大学城规划 |中国劳工布告栏 星期一, 2026 年 11 月 2 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港特首和教育部长讨论大学城计划 香港行政长官会见了中国教育部长，并概述了北领地建设“大学城”的计划，以吸引顶尖机构和人才。香港旨在提升香港的全球教育地位并深化跨境学术合作。香港行政长官李家港会见中国教育部部长王锦彪
content:
香港特首与教育部长讨论大学城规划 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港特首与教育部长讨论大学城规划
香港特首会见了中国教育部长，并概述了北领地建设“大学城”的计划，以吸引顶尖机构和人才。香港旨在提升香港的全球教育地位并深化跨境学术合作。
政府宣布，香港行政长官李家超于 2026 年 11 月 2 日会见了中国教育部部长王锦彪。李显龙对部长表示欢迎，并重点介绍了香港有五所世界排名前 100 的大学，使香港跻身全球教育领导者之列。
李说，政府正在实施第一个五年教育计划，将香港打造成全球高端人才的中心。他补充说，针对海外学生的专门计划和首届“香港留学周”，以有史以来规模最大的亚太国际教育协会年会为特色，都展示了香港的高等教育影响力。
李说，在“一国两制”原则下，香港将继续开展“香港：你的世界级校园”国际活动，并支持本地院校在内地和海外举办招聘活动，扩大人才库。
李说，该市正在加快北领地或“北城”的发展，以大学城为中心，集教育、科技、产业、人才和城市发展于一体。这一模式推动政府、产业、学术、研究和投资之间的合作，为高等教育和创新打造战略基地。政府将与教育部合作，吸引更多内地顶尖大学和研究机构落户北领地，汇聚学术和研究优势，实现互利共赢。
李指出，大湾区内的高等教育关系密切，他表示，所有八所公帑资助的香港大学均在深圳设立产学基地，并在内地城市设有四个校区。今年是粤港澳大学联盟成立十周年，政府将优化联盟机制，深化创新和人才交流。李说，在部长级支持下，香港与内地将加强师资培训、数码教育、爱国主义教育等领域的合作，助力教育强国建设。

Hong Kong leader and education minister discuss university city plan | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 2 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong leader and education minister discuss university city plan
Hong Kong's chief executive met China's education minister and outlined plans for a 'university city' in the Northern Territory to attract top institutions and talent. The city aims to boost Hong Kong's global education standing and deepen cross-border academic collaboration.
Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee met China's Education Minister Wang Jinpiao on 2 November 2026, the government announced. Lee welcomed the minister and highlighted Hong Kong's five world top-100 universities, placing the city among global education leaders.
The government is implementing its first five-year education plan to turn Hong Kong into a hub for high-end global talent, Lee said. A dedicated scheme for overseas students and the inaugural 'Study in Hong Kong Week', featuring the largest-ever Asia-Pacific International Education Association annual conference, are showcasing the city's higher education influence, he added.
Under the 'one country, two systems' principle, Hong Kong will continue its 'Hong Kong: Your World-class Campus' international campaign and support local institutions in recruiting events on the mainland and overseas to expand the talent pool, Lee stated.
Lee said the city is accelerating development of the Northern Territory, or 'North City', centred on a university city that integrates education, technology, industry, talent and urban development. This model drives collaboration among government, industry, academia, research and investment to create a strategic base for higher education and innovation. The government will work with the education ministry to attract more top mainland universities and research institutes to the Northern Territory, pooling academic and research strengths for mutual benefit.
Noting close higher-education ties within the Greater Bay Area, Lee said all eight publicly funded Hong Kong universities have set up industry-academia bases in Shenzhen, with four operating campuses in mainland cities. As the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau University Alliance marks its tenth anniversary this year, the government will optimise alliance mechanisms to deepen innovation and talent exchanges. With ministerial support, Hong Kong and the mainland will enhance cooperation in teacher training, digital education and patriotic education to help build a strong education nation, Lee said.

content:
《堅不可摧-神韻背後的故事》紀錄片，11/1日在雲林縣斗六市三好國際酒店播映，引起觀賞者很迴響，國際扶輪資深社員蔡涵霖（前排左四），非常感佩神韻演員堅守傳統文化的勇氣！（廖素貞／大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月04日訊】（大紀元記者廖素貞台灣雲林報導）一部沉痛卻充滿力量的紀錄片《堅不可摧-神韻背後的故事》，11月1日在雲林縣斗六市三好國際酒店播映，引起民眾很大的震撼，受訪民眾在看完影片後，情緒難掩激動，有對中共暴政的憤慨，更有對神韻藝術團及其家屬無比的敬佩與深沉的反思。這不單單是一場關於藝術與迫害的記錄，更是一場關於個人良知、國家主權與家庭價值的深刻拷問。
「為什麼一個弘揚中華文化的藝術團總部，竟然是在美國，而不是在中華文化發源的地方？」國際扶輪資深社員蔡涵霖開門見山地提出了這項令人汗顏的質疑。
她說，神韻藝術團以弘揚中華五千年傳統文化為宗旨，卻在中國大陸遭受殘酷的打壓與迫害。藝術團被迫將訓練總部設於美國紐約，才得以在自由的土地上將這份珍貴的文化發揚光大、巡迴全球。
蔡女士感嘆，面對這群在海外默默守護傳統文化的藝術家，每一個台灣人與華人都應該感到汗顏與反思：「人家在幫你宣揚傳統文化，你不但沒有感謝，竟然還想盡辦法去迫害它！」這種荒謬的現實，也讓人深刻體會到自由的可貴。
紀錄片中揭露了中共為了阻止神韻演出所採取的極端手段，包含發送恐怖郵件、揚言設置炸彈、用槍掃射，甚至對主持人與團員進行極其殘忍且喪心病狂的人身威脅。她痛心表示，這些藝術家只是單純透過頂尖的舞蹈與音樂傳遞善良，卻要面臨如此殘暴的恐嚇。「這簡直比魔鬼還要可怕！」
「更令人敬佩的是藝術家與其背後家庭的韌性」蔡女士特別提到，這些藝術家的父母與家人，在孩子巡迴演出期間，必須承受著多大的壓力與看不見的危險，但他們沒有退縮，依然勇敢地支持孩子站上國際舞台。這份凌駕於恐懼之上的勇氣，太令人感動了！
談到台灣當前的處境與社會現狀，蔡女士分享了自己的家庭對話。在今年參加法輪功的悼念活動時，她的兒子堅定地說：「媽媽，你看這一群勇敢的人，我們不可以離開，我們要跟他們站在最後一刻，親自對他們說聲謝謝，謝謝他們的勇敢，謝謝他們守護台灣。」
她直言，如果大家面對暴政不敢站出來，甚至有人想要將台灣賣給別人，那麼下一代將生活在怎樣的環境中？「如果你不守護好你的家園與良知，你的下一代就會生活在暴政與不安全底下。」她呼籲，守護這一切不只是為了「國家」，更是為了自己的家庭與孩子。因此每個人都應該站出來出一份力，支持並保護這樣傳播善良與正義的藝術團體。
對於這群在最前線苦練、在極權威脅下依然堅持前行的藝術家們，蔡女士表示，買票觀賞演出不僅僅是對神韻的一份支持，更是對他們的一種「敬意」。所以她已買了四張衛武營的票，準備和家人一起去觀賞，也會鼓勵親朋好友一起去看！
《堅不可摧》不僅記錄了神韻藝術團背後的艱辛與輝煌，更像是一面鏡子，照出了極權的醜陋，也照亮了人性的光輝。唯有更多人認清真相、勇敢站出來，良善與自由才能在這片土地上生生不息。
斗六市民代表會副主席祕書黃姿琳也到場觀賞，她表示，片中最令人感動的是神韻演員堅忍不拔的精神，並讚賞神韻藝術學院培養學生面對逆境時，要堅定信念。（廖素貞／大紀元）
斗六市民代表會副主席祕書黃姿琳也到場觀賞，她表示，片中最令人感動的是神韻演員堅忍不拔的精神，並讚賞神韻藝術學院培養學生面對逆境時，要堅定信念，她鼓勵所有演員只要內心足夠強大，便能無所畏懼地面對任何困難與挑戰。
曾帶高齡母親觀賞演出的她，非常佩服神韻以藝術形式弘揚「忠孝節義、禮義廉恥」傳統文化。這和縣府推動「禮義廉恥」的品德教育不謀而和，她認為教育應從小扎根品德，並提到自己與身為獅子會成員的妹妹，長期投入公益與教育界服務，同時也發動獅友與家庭一起支持神韻演出。
前同濟會主席陳添壽在觀賞紀錄片後，大讚神韻幕後團隊堅持不懈的精神，並提到片中兩位學生的父母，擔心自己的孩子在巡迴演出過程中，會不會受到傷害而憂心，讓同為父母的他感同身受。（廖素貞／大紀元）
前同濟會主席陳添壽在觀賞紀錄片後，大讚神韻幕後團隊堅持不懈的精神，並提到片中兩位學生的父母，擔心自己的孩子在巡迴演出過程中，會不會受到傷害而憂心，讓同為父母的他感同身受。
他強調，弘揚中華傳統文化與品德教育的藝術團體，絕不容許被破壞與打壓，大家應大力推廣支持！並分享自己每年會買票帶家人觀賞，且長期透過社服團體，支持雲林在地學校的發展，如蔦松藝術學校！
面對中共的攻擊，他鼓勵表演藝術家們不用怕要繼續前進，同時呼籲全民支持神韻，並期盼縣府能興建國家級表演廳，讓當地的孩子與鄉親能在雲林就可欣賞世界級藝術演出。◇

Japanese equities sank amid indications of Democratic gains in Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, a scenario some strategists had said would weigh on artificial intelligence stocks.
The tech-heavy Nikkei 225 declined as much as 4.8%, with chip and AI-related shares from memory maker Kioxia Holdings to MLCC maker Taiyo Yuden slumping more than 13% and among the worst performers. The broader Topix index fell as much as 3.5%.
“Global equity markets have already begun pricing in the view that a Democratic advantage would create headwinds for AI-related stocks,” said Masahiro Yamaguchi, head of investment research at SMBC Trust Bank.

content:
工资动荡考验孟加拉国服装业的低成本优势海峡时报
工资动荡考验孟加拉国服装业的低成本优势
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
11 月 4 日，孟加拉国达卡米尔普尔，制衣工人在工厂外举行抗议活动，要求提高工资，安保人员在站岗。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 4 日 下午 04:15
更新于 2026 年 11 月 4 日，下午 04:15
孟加拉国服装业面临薪资抗议。工人们希望加薪 140%，达卡附近的工厂已经停止生产。
骚乱扰乱了 H&M、Primark 和沃尔玛等品牌的订单。 Sparrow Group 工厂发生袭击，迫使 5,000 多名工人撤离。
较高的工资可能会削弱孟加拉国的低成本优势。政府成立了工资委员会，而买家和工厂则警告称，延误、成本上升和利润微薄会增加风险。
达卡 — — 低工资和进入主要西方市场的免税准入帮助孟加拉国成为仅次于中国的全球第二大服装出口国，但针对工资的抗议正在考验这个占该国出口收入 80% 以上的行业的成本优势。
10月31日，首都达卡周边工业区爆发抗议活动，迫使数百家服装厂暂停生产。工人们要求加薪 140%，并与警方发生冲突，警方使用了催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹。
这场骚乱发生之际，拥有 400 万名员工、以低成本和可靠性着称的服装行业即将开始为 H&M、Primark 和 Walmart 等主要品牌生产春季系列，并暴露出随着全球竞争加剧而提高工资的挑战。
服装公司高管表示，在中东战争和 2024 年大规模反政府抗议导致燃料和电力严重短缺造成早些时候的中断之后，忧心忡忡的客户已经打电话询问发货事宜。
Sparrow Group的客户包括Zara、Gap和Marks & Spencer，该集团表示，在大批人群袭击其工厂后，该集团已于11月2日停止生产。
闭路电视录像显示，人们在试图强行打开大门时投掷砖块和石块，砸碎窗户并损坏外墙。 Sparrow 负责人 Shovon Islam 表示，5000 多名工人已安全疏散。目前尚不清楚谁是此次袭击的幕后黑手。
Islam 告诉路透社，“这是该行业最繁忙的季节”，并补充说主要发货时间定于 11 月。
“现阶段的任何中断都极具破坏性，并且会在最糟糕的情况下阻碍生产。我所有的买家都很担心。”
工人们希望将最低月工资从目前的 12,500 塔卡（12,500 塔卡）提高到 30,000 塔卡（310 新元）。上一次加薪是在2023年，当时工资上涨了56%以上。此前的涨幅在 50% 至 77% 之间。
孟加拉国劳工和就业部秘书阿卜杜尔·拉赫曼·塔拉夫德尔 (Abdur Ra​​hman Tarafder) 表示，孟加拉国政府于 11 月 1 日成立了工资委员会，在考虑通货膨胀、经济状况、生活成本和出口表现等因素后提出薪酬建议。
包括该行业顶尖美国公司在内的美国服装和鞋类协会表示，该委员会是“提供公平工资的重要机会，使服装工人能够养活自己和家人”，并呼吁进行年度审查。
服装业约占孟加拉国GDP的10%。
任何与过去类似的增长都可能使孟加拉国的最低工资高于印度，而印度是世界上最低工资水平最高的国家。

Wage unrest tests Bangladesh garment industry’s low-cost edge | The Straits Times
Wage unrest tests Bangladesh garment industry’s low-cost edge
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Security personnel stand guard as garment workers stage a protest outside a factory to demand higher wages in Mirpur, Dhaka, in Bangladesh on Nov 4.
Published Nov 04, 2026, 04:15 PM
Updated Nov 04, 2026, 04:15 PM
Bangladesh’s garment industry faces protests over pay. Workers want a 140% rise, and factories have stopped production near Dhaka.
The unrest has disrupted orders for brands like H&M, Primark and Walmart. A factory attack at Sparrow Group forced evacuation of more than 5,000 workers.
Higher wages could weaken Bangladesh’s low-cost edge. The government has formed a wage board, while buyers and factories warn that delays, rising costs and thin margins add risk.
DHAKA – Low wages and duty-free access to key Western markets helped Bangladesh become the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China, but protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings.
Protests began on Oct 31 in industrial areas around the capital Dhaka, forcing hundreds of garment factories to suspend production. Workers are demanding a 140% wage hike and have clashed with police, who used tear gas and sound grenades.
The unrest comes as the garment industry, which employs 4 million people and is known for its low costs and reliability, was about to begin manufacturing spring collections for major brands such as H&M, Primark and Walmart, and exposes the challenge of raising wages as global competition intensifies.
Garment company executives say worried clients have already called about shipments, after earlier disruptions from severe fuel and power shortages from the Middle East war and 2024’s mass anti-government protests.
Sparrow Group, whose clients include Zara, Gap and Marks & Spencer, said it halted production on Nov 2 after a large crowd attacked its factory.
CCTV footage showed people throwing bricks and stones, smashing windows and damaging exterior walls while attempting to force open the main gates. Sparrow head Shovon Islam said more than 5,000 workers were evacuated safely. It was not immediately clear who was behind the attack.
“This is the industry’s busiest season,” Islam told Reuters, adding major shipments were scheduled for November.
“Any disruption at this stage is extremely damaging and is hampering production at the worst possible time. All my buyers are concerned.”
Workers want a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (S$310), from 12,500 taka currently. The last pay increase was in 2023 when wages went up by more than 56%. Previous hikes were between 50% and 77%.
Bangladesh’s government formed a wage board on Nov 1 to make a pay recommendation after considering factors including inflation, economic conditions, living costs and export performance, said Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
The American Apparel & Footwear Association, which includes the top US companies in the sector, said the board was a “critical opportunity to deliver a fair wage that allows garment workers to support themselves and their families” and called for an annual review process.
The garment industry contributes about 10% of Bangladesh’s GDP.
Any increase that is similar to past raises could push Bangladesh’s minimum wage above India, the world’s fourth-largest textile exporter.
Industry officials say minimum garment sector wages in India typically range from 13,000 rupees (S$175) to 15,000 rupees a month. Pay in China and Vietnam is roughly twice as much as in Bangladesh, according to 2024 data from the International Labour Organization.
M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, chief executive of Clifton Group, a garment company in Bangladesh’s port city of Chittagong, said India was also an increasingly strong competitor because it had its own cotton and a strong yarn industry, as well as government incentives to support the industry.
And while Bangladesh enjoys duty-free and quota-free access to places including the EU, Britain and Canada, India now has a free trade deal with the UK, the second-biggest destination for Bangladeshi garments.
In the financial year ended June 30, Bangladesh’s garment export earnings fell 1.65% from a year earlier to US$38.70 billion (S$49.48 billion), though they rebounded 6.1% in July-September to US$10.58 billion.
Chowdhury said an American buyer recently sought a 3-cent reduction per piece on a knitwear order after Indian manufacturers offered lower prices.
“We had no choice but to accept,” he said, even as logistics costs rose 5% to 7% over the past year due to higher fuel, electricity, shipping and freight expenses.
“Costs are rising from all sides, but buyers are still pushing for lower prices,” Chowdhury said.
“With margins often limited to 2% to 3%, factories have little room to absorb additional costs. Worker demands are understandable, but prolonged disruptions could threaten jobs and factory viability.”
Labour currently makes up about 10% to 13% of the industry’s costs.
Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said buyers valued reliability.
“A slightly cheaper supplier can quickly become more expensive if orders are delayed, quality is inconsistent, or labour unrest repeatedly interrupts production,” he said. REUTERS

title: 美國中期選舉民調：選民最關心經濟與民主現況

content:
Play video, "BBC asks voters across US what brought them to the polls today", 節目全長 0,34
音頻加註文字，觀看：BBC在全美各地訪問選民：是什麼促使他們今天前往投票？（英文影片）
Author, 克莉絲汀·傑文斯（Christine Jeavans）
根據選舉日民調，美國選民最關心的議題是經濟和民主現況。
這項正式名稱為「選民民調」（Voter Poll）的調查，訪問了數以萬計的美國選民，了解他們的看法與投票動機，並按年齡、性別、教育程度等人口特徵進行分析。
民調公司SSRS受多家新聞機構組成的聯盟委託蒐集數據。這項調查以具有代表性的美國選民樣本為基礎，涵蓋選前調查，以及對提前投票和當天投票選民的出口民調。
以下是2026年選民民調的部分結果。和所有民調一樣，這些數據均為估計值，且隨著更多資料陸續進來，相關數字仍可能更新。
在超過7.9萬人參與的調查中，39%的受訪者表示經濟是最重要議題；32%則認為民主現況最為重要。
其後依序為移民議題（14%）。至於醫療保健、外交政策與犯罪問題，認為是首要議題的選民比例則較低。
75%的受訪者認為經濟狀況「不太好或糟糕」；只有25%認為「很好或優秀」。
至於自身家庭財務情況，44%表示比兩年前更差，38%表示差不多，18%則表示有所改善。
接受調查的選民中，接近三分之二（65%）認為美國總統特朗普的政策讓美國經濟狀況惡化。
相比之下，28%認為特朗普的政策改善了經濟狀況，僅8%認為他沒有造成任何影響。
調查同時詢問，支持或反對特朗普是否是他們此次投票的原因之一。
43%的受訪者表示，表達對特朗普的反對是投票原因之一；41%則表示特朗普並非影響因素。僅16%表示，支持特朗普是他們投票的原因。
38%的受訪者表示，對美國目前的發展方向感到憤怒；另有37%表示不滿。
換言之，多數受訪選民向SSRS表示，他們對國家的現況並不滿意。
另外，高達90%的受訪者表示，政府腐敗是影響其投票的重要或關鍵因素。
除了較宏觀的議題外，調查也詢問了通膨與物價上漲對民眾生活的影響。
將近八成（79%）選民表示，過去一年來通膨對自己及家人造成嚴重或中度困難。
59%的選民表示，對汽油與柴油價格感到「非常擔憂」；58%則對食品與日用品價格表達同樣程度的憂慮。
62%的受訪者認為，高於正常水準的物價主要與特朗普的政策有關。
38%則認為，較大程度是受到其無法控制的外部因素影響。
這項民調還顯示，約六成受訪者（62%）認為，美國對伊朗採取軍事行動是一項錯誤決定。
另外，74%的選民表示，此一衝突是影響其國會投票的重要或關鍵因素。
全國數據顯示，57%的女性支持民主黨眾議院候選人，支持共和黨者為41%。男性選民則較為平均，兩黨支持度均接近五成。
按年齡區分，45歲以下選民中，接近三分之二表示投票給民主黨。45至64歲的中年選民則呈現五五波，49%支持民主黨，48%支持共和黨。
65歲以上選民中，略多於半數表示支持共和黨候選人；47%支持民主黨。
根據估計，全國白人選民有51%投票給共和黨，47%支持民主黨。
其他族群則較傾向支持民主黨。其中西語裔與拉丁裔選民約有60%支持民主黨，35%支持共和黨。
調查顯示，未接受大學教育的選民較傾向支持共和黨，比例為51%對45%。擁有大學學歷的選民則以61%對36%的比例支持民主黨。
不過，上述數據反映的是全國整體趨勢，各州的投票模式仍可能有所差異。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

zh_title: 如何防止台湾能源检疫
summary: 如何防止台湾能源检疫 - 大西洋理事会北京正在为台湾能源检疫奠定基础。经济、政治、技术和军事因素可能导致能源检疫风险在 2028 年和 2029 年达到顶峰。为了阻止这种强制行动，美国及其盟国应与台湾合作，通过支持上述所有能源战略来加强其安全，重点是向台湾北部供应用于发电的柴油。中共总书记习近平多次明确表态：
content:
如何防止台湾能源检疫 - 大西洋理事会
北京正在为台湾的能源检疫奠定基础。
经济、政治、技术和军事因素可能导致能源检疫风险在 2028 年和 2029 年达到峰值。
为了阻止这种胁迫行动，美国及其盟国应与台湾合作，通过支持上述所有能源战略来加强台湾的安全，重点是向台湾北部供应用于发电的柴油。
中国共产党总书记习近平一贯明确表示台湾应该与中国大陆“统一”，并在2013年表示“两岸长期存在的政治分歧……总不能一代一代传下去”。习近平还在 2026 年 5 月与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普会面时警告称，在台湾问题上可能会发生“冲突甚至冲突”。问题似乎不是决心问题，而是时机问题。出于政治、经济和技术原因，习近平可能对台湾采取行动的风险可能在 2028 年和 2029 年达到顶峰。
为了实现其长期的统一目标，北京可能会尝试通过非动能措施胁迫台湾。隔离的模糊性和灵活性可能使其成为对习近平特别有吸引力的选择。北京可以宣称，检疫——允许一些船只通过，同时拒绝其他船只，特别是油轮和液化天然气（LNG）运输船——是一种国内执法措施，而不是一种战争行为。有证据表明，习近平的军队已经在为隔离而不是入侵进行演练，因为中国海警在台湾以东海域持续存在，并试图将封锁商业交通正常化，从而挑战台北的海上控制。
切断台湾能源供应的隔离作为一种强制工具尤其有效。台湾几乎没有本土生产石油、天然气或煤炭，这使得它几乎完全依赖海运进口碳氢化合物。北京很早就明白能源安全在台湾突发事件中的重要性。目前，它不太容易受到能源中断的影响，并准备好承受根据需要切断部分能源进口的情况。
对台湾进行能源隔离对美国来说将是一件严重的事情。台湾因其地理位置、深厚的技术专长以及作为人工智能（AI）供应链关键节点的地位而对华盛顿具有重要的战略意义。中国吞并台湾将使全球经济和战略力量平衡向有利于北京的方向倾斜，美国决策者必须避免对台湾采取强制行动，否则可能升级为军事冲突。碰撞的危险怎么强调都不为过：美国和中国都是拥有强大常规军队的核武器国家；技术超级大国，尤其是人工智能领域；以及拥有一系列强制工具的庞大经济体。
应对这些风险需要大量军事投资，但联盟决策者不应忽视近期能源隔离的严重风险。为了阻止台湾的能源隔离，美国和其他民主国家应与台湾合作，通过上述所有方法以及快速部署燃料来源（特别是柴油）的战略优先事项来加强其能源安全。美国，T

How to prevent an energy quarantine of Taiwan - Atlantic Council
Beijing is laying the groundwork for an energy quarantine of Taiwan.
Economic, political, technical, and military factors could lead energy quarantine risks to peak in 2028 and 2029.
To deter this coercive action, the United States and allies should work with Taiwan to bolster its security through support for an all-of-the-above energy strategy, concentrating on supplying northern Taiwan with diesel for power generation.
Chinese Communist Party (CCP) General Secretary Xi Jinping has consistently made clear his view that Taiwan should be “reunified” with mainland China, stating in 2013 that “long-standing cross-Strait political differences … cannot be passed down from generation to generation (总不能一代一代传下去).” Xi also warned of “clashes or even conflicts” over Taiwan in his May 2026 meeting with US President Donald Trump. The matter appears to be a question not of determination but of timing. For political, economic, and technical reasons, the risk that Xi might move against Taiwan could peak in 2028 and 2029.
To achieve its longstanding unification goal, Beijing might attempt to coerce Taiwan via non-kinetic measures. The ambiguity and flexibility of a quarantine could render it an especially attractive option for Xi. Beijing could claim that a quarantine—allowing some ships to pass while turning back others, especially oil tankers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers—is a domestic law-enforcement measure rather than an act of war. There is some evidence that Xi’s forces are already rehearsing for a quarantine rather than an invasion, as the Chinese coast guard is maintaining a continuous presence in waters east of Taiwan and trying to normalize interdictions of live commercial traffic, thereby challenging Taipei’s maritime control.
A quarantine to cut off Taiwan’s energy supply would be particularly effective as a coercive tool. Taiwan has virtually no indigenous production of oil, natural gas, or coal, rendering it almost totally reliant on seaborne imports for hydrocarbons. Beijing has long understood the importance of energy security in a Taiwan contingency. It is currently much less vulnerable to an energy outage and is prepared to weather a cutoff of some of its own energy imports as needed.
An energy quarantine of Taiwan would be a grave matter for the United States. Taiwan is strategically important to Washington due to its geography, deep technological expertise, and position as a critical node in artificial intelligence (AI) supply chains. China’s absorption of Taiwan would tilt the global economic and strategic balance of power in Beijing’s favor, making it imperative for US policymakers to avert coercive action against the island, which could escalate into a military conflict. It is difficult to overstate the dangers of a collision: the United States and China are nuclear-armed nations with powerful conventional militaries; technological superpowers, especially in AI; and huge economies with an array of coercive tools.
Countering these risks will require substantial military investments, but coalition policymakers should not overlook the serious risks of a near-term energy quarantine. To deter an energy quarantine of Taiwan, the United States and other democracies should work with Taiwan to reinforce its energy security with an all-of-the-above approach and the strategic prioritization of rapidly deployable fuel sources, especially diesel. The United States, Taiwan, and other actors should immediately begin preparing for a contingency by deploying a diesel-generation supply chain across Taiwan, especially in the energy-scarce northern regions surrounding the capital, Taipei. That will include diesel production at refineries, distributed storage, and ultimately generators for power supply. The humble diesel generator could be a key determinant in the future of global power.
The groundwork: Beijing is mitigating its own energy vulnerabilities
In 2003, then General Secretary Hu Jintao warned that China faced the “Malacca Dilemma,” or “马六甲困局.” Hu noted that Beijing’s reliance on seaborne oil imports from the Middle East navigating the Malacca Strait near Singapore raised acute vulnerabilities, as shipments could be interdicted by the US Navy. More than two decades later, Beijing is becoming increasingly self-sufficient in energy overall and in transportation fuels such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. While Beijing will not achieve true independence in transportation fuels for several years, it is on its way to effectively mitigating the Malacca Dilemma.
Beijing has been seeking to mitigate this dilemma via a combination of reduced transport fuel demand (largely from vehicle electrification), elevated domestic crude oil production, overland crude oil pipeline imports (largely from Russia), maximizing refinery production of transportation fuels, and tapping unprecedentedly large petroleum stockpiles. Beijing’s growing oil security will enable it to increasingly decouple from international markets and allow it to act more aggressively vis-à-vis Taiwan.
Electrification has been fundamental to China’s energy self-sufficiency drive. Electricity’s share of final energy in China has grown from about 5 percent in 1990 to nearly 30 percent today, an increase of about 1 percentage point every year, and will soon surpass the percentage share of every Group of Seven (G7) economy. Mainland China’s power generation capacity has risen from 138 gigawatts in 1990 to over 4,000 gigawatts by May 2026; China has also added 24.2 million charging points (not stations) and, by 2023, had already provided $230 billion in government support to its EV industry. Finally, many Chinese cities have mandated that ride share vehicles and urban logistics vehicles must be “new energy vehicles”—in practice, usually battery EVs. These measures have enabled China to become the undeniable world leader in vehicle electrification.
Vehicle electrification rapidly mitigates Beijing’s exposure to the Malacca Dilemma by directly reducing gasoline and diesel demand, especially in politically-sensitive first tier cities. According to the International Energy Agency, electric vehicles are set to reduce Chinese oil demand by about a total of 2.7 million barrels per day (MMbpd) by 2030. In a July 2025 analysis, Rhodium Group found that China’s total electric vehicle fleet already displaced more than 1 MMbpd, with battery electric vehicles beginning to make significant headway in trucking fleets that rely primarily on diesel.
For these reasons, the International Energy Agency and others hold that Chinese gasoline and diesel demand has likely already peaked. Deployment of advanced, energy-dense batteries to medium and heavy-duty vehicles would further reduce diesel consumption, alleviating Beijing’s chief transport fuel constraint in a crisis. Adoption of advanced batteries in heavy-duty vehicles might rise sharply over the next year or two.
As it reduces its transport fuel demand via vehicle electrification, China has also stockpiled about 1.2 billion barrels of crude oil in December 2025 in total petroleum reserves, by far the world’s largest. While Beijing is drawing down oil inventories amid the oil market disruptions from the US–Iran war, storage levels remain elevated and can be expanded if the conflict winds down.
In the case of a quarantine, Beijing would rely heavily on supply flows of oil, not only on stock withdrawals.
Here it’s useful to divide Beijing’s oil supplies into different resilience tiers. Tier 1, the most secure tier, is China’s own domestic crude oil production, which ticked up from 3.8 million barrels per day (MMbpd) in 2017 to about 4.4 MMbpd in the first seven months of 2026, covering about 30 percent of domestic demand before the US–Iran war.
In addition to its own domestic production, China can also obtain additional volumes from relatively secure overland pipelines in Tier 2A. China’s secure overland crude oil shipments total about 0.8 MMbpd. This is split between the Russia-to-China leg of the East Siberia–Pacific Ocean pipeline, with deliveries of about 600,000 barrels per day (b/d), and the Atasu–Alashankou pipeline, which brings both Russian and Kazakhstani oil via Kazakhstan and delivers roughly 200,000 b/d to Xinjiang. Existing Russian and Kazakhstani overland pipelines have delivery capacity of about 1.2 MMbpd; in a crisis, China would likely be able to access these full volumes, albeit at a possible premium.
Tier 2B consists of Russian maritime crude imports. Russia typically ships about 0.75 MMbpd to China from its Kozmino port, near Vladivostok, with other export terminals typically providing about 0.25 MMbpd. The US Navy and coalitional navies would weigh carefully whether to interdict Russian ships and disable Russian exports. Targeting Russian vessels and infrastructure risks horizontal and perhaps even vertical escalation, but in a Taiwan contingency the benefits of disabling Russian energy shipments to the Chinese mainland could, under some conditions, outweigh that risk. To mitigate the risks of maritime transit, Beijing and Moscow might expand the capacity of the mainland China leg of the East Siberia–Pacific Ocean pipeline, “promoting” perhaps 0.8 MMbpd from Tier 2B into Tier 2A.
Tier 3 is the 200,000 b/d pipeline from Myanmar, which delivers oil to Yunnan. This source can be thought of as only quasi-overland, however, as it relies on maritime imports to the Made Island oil import terminal that could be interdicted relatively easily.
Tier 4 imports, meanwhile, consist of all other maritime sources.
China can reliably access about 5.6 MMbpd of crude oil supply from domestic and overland sources if all existing pipeline capacity is utilized. Adding about another 1 MMbpd from Russian maritime imports would bring the total to nearly 6.6 MMbpd. If its most secure supplies are operable in a crisis, then about 30 percent of China’s supplies would hinge on Russia, demonstrating Beijing’s interest in maintaining close ties with Moscow.
Turning to demand, China’s refinery runs for crude oil stood at about 15.2 MMbpd in January–February 2026 (assuming 7.33 barrels/ton). Amid the US–Iran war, these runs fell to about 12.5 MMbpd in June, per China’s National Bureau of Statistics. In a contingency, Beijing could again sharply reduce its demand, including in petrochemicals, which accounts for about 25 percent of Chinese oil demand and largely serves the export market. In addition, Beijing could order refineries to maximize output of transportation fuels, including diesel and jet fuel for its military.
Given that total domestic supply from production and secure import capacity equals 6.6 MMbpd, and assuming total refinery runs of 12.5 MMbpd seen in June 2026, China would face a daily deficit of about 5.9 MMbpd in a contingency today. Assuming that China has reserves of about 1.1 billion barrels of crude oil after Iran war-related drawdowns, and that it would be able to draw inventories to only 20 percent before facing constraints from geographic dispersion and tank draw, China would be able to sustain at least one hundred and fifty days of civilian and military activities before reaching physical shortage.
By 2030, however, Beijing will very likely enjoy far greater oil security. Tier 1 and 2A overland crude supplies could very easily rise to 6.8 MMbpd on higher domestic production and greater overland tie-ins with Russian and Central Asian crude oil pipelines. Crude oil demand, meanwhile, could fall to 11.5 MMbpd amid vehicle electrification, leaving a deficit of 4.7 MMbpd. Assuming 1.2 billion barrels of crude oil reserves and a maximum drawdown of inventories to 20 percent, Beijing could likely cover at least two hundred days of refinery runs in a contingency by 2030. Beijing may soon be able to withstand an oil blockade for well over half a year, and perhaps much longer if it continues to increase the size of its oil reserves, can still access Russian maritime imports, or accelerates vehicle electrification.
The United States’ implicit answer to a potential Taiwan quarantine has been to impose a counter-blockade of China’s oil imports. That strategy is increasingly outdated. Policymakers in Washington, Taipei, Tokyo, and beyond need to understand this dangerous new reality, insulate against an energy quarantine, and find other sources of coercive leverage against Beijing.
Taiwan’s exposure: Two likely scenarios for an energy quarantine
Taiwan’s indigenous energy production (including nuclear energy generation) as a percentage of all energy demand declined from 8.3 percent to 5.3 percent from 2016 to 2025.
Taiwan’s reserves of oil, coal, and LNG are required to cover ninety days, thirty days, and eleven days of consumption for each commodity, respectively, although inventories typically cover more. In March 2026, the Ministry of Economic Affairs reported oil, coal, and LNG on-hand inventories of one hundred and fifty days, forty days, and eleven days, respectively. Still, Taiwan’s actual days of consumption covered vary based on several factors, including seasonal weather patterns, its ability to export goods such as semiconductors from its energy-intensive industrial sector, and the continued operation of refineries.
Other regional democracies’ roles in a Taiwan contingency could be constrained by their energy-related vulnerabilities. Japan and South Korea also have limited storage inventories, while other US allies such as the Philippines and Australia are themselves highly reliant on energy imports. Australia’s fuel dependency is staggering: it relies on imports for 83 percent of all refined petroleum products. The coalition has serious work to do to improve its collective energy resilience, and to do so quickly.
If Beijing attempted to subjugate Taiwan via an energy quarantine, two scenarios are most likely. Beijing might straightforwardly implement a quarantine or even blockade of Taiwan, attempting to interdict any inbound energy shipments via its coast guard by claiming a legal pretext.
Alternatively, Beijing might try an indirect approach by exploiting or even stimulating a future Middle Eastern oil crisis. Surging oil prices would disproportionately damage Beijing’s regional rivals, which are relatively reliant on oil imports even as China increasingly turns into a self-sufficient electrotech state.
Timing the risk: Quarantine dangers might peak in 2028 and 2029
The dangers of an energy-weighted geopolitical crisis over Taiwan are already serious but might peak in 2028 and 2029 due to economics, politics, Taiwan’s electricity reserve margins, military readiness, and AI. Mainland China’s economy is showing significant strain even as Taiwan’s powers ahead; both Taiwan and the United States will hold key elections in 2028; Taiwan’s electricity reserve margin is on track to reach dangerously low levels in this period; US military readiness levels might be damaged by protracted deployments in other theaters; and while AI timelines are highly unpredictable, the United States might begin to experience takeoff growth, which could enable it to establish permanent technological dominance. Given these factors, and his own age, Xi might believe by 2028 that he has a limited window of opportunity to act.
Beijing has economic reasons for attempting to control Taiwan sooner rather than later. If economic trends continue, Beijing’s comparative performance legitimacy will weaken vis-à-vis Taiwan through January 2028. Taiwan’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth is projected to reach an astonishing 11 percent in 2026. While most economic growth is concentrated in the tech sector, real median incomes are rising, Taiwan’s government is flush enough to disburse cash payments, the fiscal budget is balanced, and Taiwan’s debt-to-GDP ratio is the lowest in East Asia. Taiwan’s economy is doing well, even if growth will likely decelerate.
Conversely, while Beijing retains formidable economic power, mainland China’seconomy shows significant weakness. Growth rates are undeniably slowing. Chinese debt levels are in a “league of their own,” according to Mark Williams, chief Asia economist at Capital Economics. Logan Wright, partner at Rhodium Group, warns that Beijing’s growth model is “fundamentally broken” and faces “steady decay.” The risks to mainland China’s economy may provide added urgency for Xi to pursue an energy quarantine of Taiwan and coerce it into accepting Beijing’s rule. Assuming current economic trends continue, Taiwan’s living standards will further outpace mainland China’s, significantly damaging the appeal of unification for Taiwan’s voters.
Taiwan will hold its next presidential election in January 2028. While nothing is certain, the outcome of the election is likely to lead to intense discomfort in Beijing (as the author has been warning since June 2026). In most democracies, rising living standards benefit the incumbent party. That means that the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) is likely to prevail in 2028 presidential elections, assuming Taiwan maintains robust economic growth, which is likely; the DPP is also favored to obtain a majority in the Legislative Yuan, Taiwan’s parliament. Living standards are not the only variable affecting elections, and the composition of candidates from the three main parties in Taiwan will matter greatly for the 2028 election, governing, and cross-Strait relations. Nonetheless, initial indications suggest that political economy trends in Taiwan do not appear to be moving in Beijing’s favor.
As political economy theory might predict, Taiwan’s voters may be rewarding the incumbent party for producing rising living standards. In a stunning reversal from even a few months ago, the DPP is now favored to win the Taipei mayoral race. The approval rating of President Lai Ching-te of the DPP has steadily climbed for months and is at its highest level since April 2025. Other parties could still win in 2028, especially if economic growth falters, perhaps due to an AI market correction in the United States. Nonetheless, assuming robust (and reasonably well-distributed) economic growth continues, then the DPP will likely win both the presidential and the Legislative Yuan elections in January 2028, to Beijing’s immense dissatisfaction.
The United States will also hold its own presidential election in November 2028. Political trends indicate the election will be divisive, potentially distracting Americans from cross-Strait affairs. In addition, while Beijing eyes Trump warily, CCP leaders believe Trump’s transactional approach to governing might offer opportunities vis-à-vis Taiwan in the remainder of his term.
Technical factors will amplify political and economic risks. Taipower, Taiwan’s state-run power company, projects that its nighttime reserve margin will fall to about 8 percent in 2028 and 2029, far below its targeted reserve margin of 15 percent. If current trends continue, Taiwan’s power sector could face interrupted power supplies at night even in peacetime, which would make it even more vulnerable to a potential energy quarantine.
Beijing will also be weighing US military readiness and weapons inventory levels. Where these will stand in 2028 is uncertain, especially if the US conflict in Iran escalates.
AI timelines are their own huge source of uncertainty for 2028–2029. Beijing’s perception that the United States might be on the verge of establishing permanent technological dominance via powerful AI might upend Xi’s assumptions about the desirability of strategic patience and further incentivize Xi to intervene against Taiwan, the world’s most advanced chipmaker.
Finally, there is the human element: Xi’s own sense of destiny. If Taiwan shows no medium-term interest in peacefully or semi-peacefully uniting with the mainland, then Xi might feel pressure to act. He will turn seventy-five in 2028, will have limited patience for sentiment to change through future Taiwanese elections in 2032 or even 2036, and has made clear he does not want the Taiwan issue ‘passed down from generation to generation.’
All these considerations do not guarantee that 2028–2029 will be the peak period of risks in US-China relations. Risks might persist for decades. Still, these factors suggest a convergence of serious, compounding risks that warrant preparation and mitigation.
A strategy for deterrence: Taiwan and its friends should prepare for an energy contingency
There is a need to hedge against the foreseeable and highly consequential risk of an energy quarantine of Taiwan by Beijing, perhaps as early as 2028. While Taiwan is already taking important steps to enhance its energy resilience, its government and the United States must do more to prepare for this risk—and quickly.
To address its urgent energy security challenges, Taiwan needs to take an all-of-the-above approach to electricity generation while bolstering transmission.
Nuclear energy, in particular, is one of the most important pillars of Taiwan’s energy resiliency and should be expanded. Nuclear energy can operate continuously for at least eighteen months once fueled. Additionally, reactors are unlikely to be deliberately destroyed by CCP forces in a contingency. Beijing does not want to risk radiation exposure on the island it seeks to seize. Working with the United States, Japan, and other actors, Taiwan should seek to expand nuclear energy capacity as quickly as possible and start bringing its third nuclear power plant in Maanshan back online in 2028.
In addition to nuclear energy, Taiwan should expand use of LNG, renewables, oil for generation and transportation, and even coal where appropriate. Taiwan should continue to deepen ties with the US LNG complex; expanding natural gas storage capacity will also prove useful.
Finally, and most importantly, the island should adopt a “north diesel, south renewables” approach to electricity generation in preparation for a contingency, and resource this plan effectively.
Northern Taiwan, home to the capital Taipei, is critical. While northern Taiwan has some limited generation capacity, it is a net “importer” from the southern and central parts of the island, in what officials call ”南電北送,”or “send southern power north.” In a contingency, northern Taiwan might not be able to access power generation from the southern and central regions due to sabotage of power stations, substations, transmission lines, or other infrastructure. Moreover, northern Taiwan cannot rely on local renewables generation: Taipei’s solar capacity factor is, inadequately, about the same as Seattle’s, onshore land availability to build more solar is minimal, and regional offshore wind projects, while useful, generate less power in peak summer electricity demand months and also face sabotage risks. Finally, gas-fired power plants at Datan and Tunghsiao constitute the bulk of northern Taiwan’s indigenous power generation, and northern Taiwan’s LNG inventories are finite. If south-to-north transmission lines are cut in a contingency, Taipei could run out of electricity in under one month.
Fuels, especially diesel, are therefore critical for countering an energy quarantine or blockade of Taiwan, particularly one that could occur on a short timeline before the island has time to strengthen resilience through nuclear energy expansion and other tactics. Diesel can be stored for long periods of time and can provide distributed power without transmission wires, as Ukraine is proving. Additionally, diesel units can be deployed in a matter of weeks, although deploying this systematically will require more time and resources.
For approximately $10 billion in up-front capital expenditure plus an estimated $500 million a year to maintain, test, and rotate fuel, northern Taiwan could field about 2 gigawatts of diesel generation (based on author calculations). About half of the capital expenditures would be for a dedicated diesel fuel stockpile and dispersed, hardened storage; generators would account for the rest of the initial outlay. That level of diesel generation would provide enough power to keep hospitals, cooling stations, sanitation, telecom, and emergency services running in northern Taiwan for roughly five months without any power from the south. Taiwan could very likely stand up a first tranche of this system by summer 2027, when it could conduct power generation exercises as part of the Urban Resilience drills. The full buildout could be completed across 2028 and 2029 (and accelerated as needed).
In addition, Taiwan’s southern and central regions have large existing thermal generation power plants along with good-to-excellent renewable resources that cannot be interdicted easily, as they are less reliant on vulnerable, long-distance transmission lines and infrastructure that carry power north. In addition to strengthening the resilience of thermal power plants, including by stockpiling coal and natural gas reserves, Taiwan should increase construction of onshore solar and wind resources in the southern and central regions. Distributed renewables generation is much more difficult to take offline by Chinese forces in a quarantine, blockade, siege, or invasion.
With diesel generation in the north, generation from coal, gas, and nuclear power plants in the south, distributed renewables throughout the island, and aggressive rationing, Taiwan could extend its ability to endure an energy blockade from mere weeks to months.
Taiwan need not act alone, however. The United States has a critical role to play in averting a Taiwan energy contingency. US firms should engage with counterparts in Taiwan across all parts of the energy supply chain, including diesel generators and storage, LNG infrastructure, nuclear energy know-how, and solar and energy storage systems. The chief US contribution to Taiwan’s energy infrastructure might be preventing sabotage. In a contingency, CCP intelligence services would likely seek to degrade or disable Taiwan’s south-to-north power transmission lines and other energy infrastructure with either cyber or kinetic means. To accomplish kinetic sabotage, CCP intelligence services would use the full spectrum of their assets, including their connections with criminal networks. Accordingly, the United States should rotate a far greater number of energy, counternarcotics, and countersabotage personnel through Taiwan, drawing on the Department of Energy, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and other civilian security agencies, through the American Institute in Taiwan.
China’s vulnerabilities: Leverage that could enforce stability
In addition to precautionary defensive measures, Washington, Taipei, and other actors should find other forms of leverage over Beijing. China’s food vulnerabilities are significant, while its steel industry relies extensively on Australian iron ore imports. Analysts should carefully scrutinize these commodities, especially if China begins to build inventories.
The most effective form of leverage vis-à-vis Beijing, however, could be economic and financial. China’s economic growth model might be broken. China remains highly reliant on other countries absorbing its overcapacity, as net exports’ contribution to GDP growth stood at 32.7 percent, the highest level since 1997. Far from successfully rebalancing, China’s economic and financial model has become more reliant on exports, investments, and debt, raising the likelihood of a painful correction. If Beijing attempted to coerce Taiwan, including through an energy quarantine, China’s ability to reach export markets might be imperiled due to a combination of economic, financial, cyber, and other measures. If China loses substantial access to export markets due to an unwise attempt to coerce Taipei, the risks for its economic, financial, social, and ultimately political stability could be profound.
While the risks of an energy quarantine are significant and rising, Taipei and Washington are well positioned to mitigate these dangers. Taiwan is already making great strides in enhancing its energy resilience. It should build on these efforts by building new generation for the long term and, especially, leveraging diesel as a near-term bridge solution. Similarly, Washington should take a more active role in opposing unilateral changes to the status quo by either side. Washington should underscore its continued commitment to the “One China” policy, anchored to the Taiwan Relations Act, the three communiqués, and the Six Assurances, while warning Beijing not to undertake aggression. If Taipei and Washington can see through this moment of danger, they could settle into a period of relative stability.
Joseph Webster is a nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council’s Global Energy Center and the Indo-Pacific Security Initiative; he also edits the independent China-Russia Report. This analysis reflects his personal opinion.

title: 美國中期選舉：民調顯示民主黨將取得勝利，但預測還準確嗎？

content:
美國中期選舉：民調顯示民主黨將取得勝利，但預測還準確嗎？ - BBC News 中文
Author, 安東尼·澤克爾（Anthony Zurcher）
民主黨帶著很高的期望迎接這場舉足輕重的美國中期選舉。
一位支持率創歷史新低的共和黨總統、對食品和各項帳單費用上漲心懷不滿的美國公眾，以及連續數月對民主黨有利的民調，都預示著週二對民主黨而言將是個美好的夜晚。
民調顯示，民主黨候選人在遠超218個議席的選區中領先，而218席正是奪取國會下院眾議院（House of Representatives）控制權所需的席位數。在關鍵的參議院（Senate）選戰中，他們與對手持平或略微領先。
《紐約時報》（New York Times）近期的一項民調顯示，南卡羅來納州（South Carolina）的參議院選戰呈現平局，而唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump）2024 年在該州領先18個百分點。有線電視新聞網（CNN）近期的調查則顯示，民主黨在得克薩斯州（Texas）、堪薩斯州（Kansas）和緬因州（Maine）領先。
美國近年的政治史上，民意調查失準的例子比比皆是，即便是在選舉前幾天進行的民調也不例外。特朗普在2016年和2024年入主白宮的過程中，表現都超出預測。2020 年，他以微弱差距落敗，而當時多數調查顯示民主黨人喬·拜登（Joe Biden）將更輕鬆獲勝。
今年早些時候，民調顯示民主黨人阿卜杜勒·埃爾-賽義德（Abdul El-Sayed）有望在密歇根州（Michigan）民主黨參議員初選中以兩位數優勢獲勝。結果差距僅為1%。在威斯康星州（Wisconsin）民主黨州長初選中，一名民調領先幅度接近20個百分點的候選人，最終以不到一個百分點的差距敗北。
Play video, "What's at stake for Trump in the US midterms?", 節目全長 0,59
進行政治和市場研究調查的益普索公共事務部（Ipsos Public Affairs）總裁克利福德·揚（Clifford Young）表示，近年來民調變得困難，原因是美國人紛紛棄用座機並過濾來電，聯繫他們更加不易。而且，民調機構聯繫到的人當中，許多人參與的意願也有所下降。
「保守派，尤其是極右翼保守派，本質上更加反建制，」揚說。 「他們什麼都不參與。他們憎恨這個體制。這就是挑戰所在。」
如果共和黨選民被系統性地低估，而民調公司在建立投票模型時沒有考慮到這一點，那麼他們的數據可能會向民主黨傾斜。
特朗普在此前總統選舉中表現超出預期，一種解釋是，他的支持者——其中許多人並非經常投票的選民——以高於預期的人數湧向投票站。
這種不可預測性是近年來幾次明顯的民調失準的主要原因之一，儘管大多數信譽良好的民調的誤差只有幾個百分點。
在勢均力敵的選戰中，這幾個百分點就可能決定候選人的勝負。而今年，許多關鍵的參議院選戰都處於這樣狹窄的差距之內。
近年來，中期選舉的大選民調已被證明更為準確，部分原因是特朗普——以及他吸引心懷不滿的美國人前往投票的獨特能力——不在選票上。
2022年，民調顯示，儘管拜登的支持率低迷，民主黨仍將打破常規預期，避免遭遇選舉慘敗。
雖然民主黨最終失去了眾議院的控制權，但差距很小，而且民主黨保住了美國參議院的控制權。
雖然今年的初選結果確實帶來了更大的意外，但揚表示，初選歷來變數較大，選民更可能在最後一刻才做出決定。不應將此視為當前這批大選民調失準的跡象。
近年來最引人注目的例子之一發生在 2010 年，當時共和黨人從民主黨手中奪得 60 多個眾議院席位，並在參議院也取得了進展。
那次選舉的背景是，經濟仍在從金融危機中艱難復甦，以及保守派對總統巴拉克·奧巴馬（Barack Obama）醫療改革的擔憂。民調曾預測民主黨會失利，但沒有預料到規模如此之大。
這次角色互換，民主黨成為反對黨，經濟議題成為選民關注的焦點。但鑑於特朗普的低支持率，民主黨的表現可能不會像歷史經驗所顯示的那樣好，也不會像一些人預期的那樣出色，原因有很多。
首先，這次選舉中涉及的大部分地區，特朗普在兩年前的總統選舉中都輕鬆拿下。對共和黨來說，這就像是主場比賽一樣。
其次，多年來眾議院選區邊界的調整，使得在兩黨之間易手的議席減少。
第三，由於國家的兩極分化加深，搖擺選民減少。一些專家形容選民群體已經僵化。
此外，共和黨一直享有資金優勢，這使他們在最後幾週有數億美元可用於投放攻擊性廣告。
Play video, "Voter voices: What issues matter most to Americans", 節目全長 1,16
民意調查模型旨在捕捉基本面的變化。精心設計的民意調查會預先考慮可能降低其可靠性的因素。
單一民調都存在固有的誤差範圍，這是基於樣本量與總體比例的統計不確定性。綜合來看，民調平均值而非單一調查結果可以提供更準確的預測。
目前來看，即使是像近幾屆總統選舉那樣的民調傾向，也顯示民主黨在11月3日晚上可能會取得不錯的成績。而且，民調失準可能偏向任何一方。在去年的州選舉和特別選舉中，民主黨的表現優於大多數民調預測，因為他們的選民投票率遠超預期。
特朗普在競選的最後幾天，在他2024年輕鬆獲勝的州舉行集會，這一景象提振了民主黨人的希望，他們認為共和黨內部民調顯示保守派候選人處境艱難。
有時，後期的轉向會改變一場選戰的態勢。有時，未決定的選民——在許多此類選戰中他們仍佔選民的重要部分——會全部倒向同一方。
在民調中，總會存在一定程度的不確定性，而管理這種不確定性，正是與科學相伴的藝術。
「我認為我們做得更好了，」揚說。 「但我們一直面臨的問題不僅僅在於民調機構，部分原因在於我們正在和人打交道。人可不是那麼容易對付的。」
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。
